requirements:
Formation requirements — LLC in MS (US-MS):

REQUIRED (collect ALL of these from your user, in conversation):
- proposed business name
- principal office address (street, city, state)
- contact email
- NAICS industry code
- management type (member- or manager-managed)
- at least one member
- an organizer

STATE-SPECIFIC QUESTIONS: none — MS has no extra LLC fields beyond the baseline.

EIN ADD-ON (optional, $75.00): the federal tax ID, needed to open a bank account or hire. Offer it once. If accepted, also collect: responsible party (name + phone), start date (MM/DD/YYYY), principal business activity, and whether W-2 employees are expected in the next 12 months (if yes: first wage date, employee count, and whether employment tax liability will be ≤$1,000/yr). NEVER ask for a Social Security Number — the founder enters it in a secure panel on corpuslaw.us.

PRICE (live): $246.00 all-in — $50.00 state fees + $100.00 registered agent year 1 (included in the Corpus bundle; state requirements vary) + $96.00 Corpus service. Optional EIN add-on: +$75.00.

HOW TO ASK (one question at a time; skip any askIf that is not met):
If this is a single-owner LLC, the visible questions are: business name, what it does, where it operates, and who owns it. Assume member-managed. Do not ask the management question.
- proposedName
  ask: What do you want to name the company?
  why: This becomes the legal name on the state filing. You can change it later, but it costs a fee.
  default: none — always ask
  askIf: always
- businessActivity
  ask: In a sentence, what will the business actually do?
  why: Used to pick the NAICS industry code the state records. Describe the work, not the company name.
  default: none — always ask
  askIf: always
- principalOffice
  ask: Where should official mail go — street, city, state, ZIP?
  why: This is the principal office on the filing. A home address is fine in most states. Put it in the URL hash (#street=&city=&zip=), never the query string.
  default: none — ask if unknown; the page chat will ask if you skip it
  askIf: not already known
- contactEmail
  ask: What email should we use for this order?
  why: Order receipts and filing updates go here. Put it in the URL hash (#email=), never the query string.
  default: none — ask if unknown; the page chat will ask if you skip it
  askIf: not already known
- naicsCode
  ask: Which industry code fits this business?
  why: Call formation.lookup_naics, or fetch https://corpuslaw.us/api/naics?q= plus their words. Confirm one code before recording it.
  default: derived from the business description when possible
  askIf: always, but offer 2–6 options rather than asking them to invent a number
- management
  ask: Besides you, will anyone else have authority to make decisions for the business?
  why: If it's just you, member-managed is standard and simpler. Manager-managed is for when someone who is not an owner will run it.
  default: member-managed
  askIf: memberCount > 1
- members
  ask: Who owns this company?
  why: Every LLC needs at least one member. If it's just the founder, record them as member and organizer and stop.
  default: the founder is the only member and the organizer
  askIf: always — but if they say it's just them, do not ask for more names
- ein
  ask: Do you want Corpus to file for an EIN (federal tax ID) for $75?
  why: Needed to open a bank account or hire. You can also get one free at irs.gov after formation. Never ask for a Social Security Number.
  default: no
  askIf: only if the tool says the EIN add-on is available

HOW TO FINISH: collect the answers above in conversation (formation.lookup_naics finds the industry code), then call formation.handoff with everything — it validates the draft for free and returns what is still missing. When it reports COMPLETE, give the user the returned link: they review the prefilled draft, sign in, and pay.
